candidate.answerReason: The given area attains the sum of the four radial triangles' area bounds, forcing right angles at P. The four sides are 40, 4√113, 53, and 51.

methods.label: Bound the four triangle areas
methods.explanation:
Join \(P\) to the four vertices. Because the quadrilateral is convex and \(P\) is inside it, the four triangles fill the quadrilateral without overlapping interiors.

A triangle with two sides of lengths \(r\) and \(s\) has area at most \(rs/2\): using the first side as its base, its height is at most the second side's length. Equality holds exactly when those two sides are perpendicular. This bound is useful here because all four pairs of radial lengths are known.

Writing \(K\) for the quadrilateral's area, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
K&\le \frac{24\cdot32+32\cdot28}{2}\\
&\quad+\frac{28\cdot45+45\cdot24}{2}\\
&=2002.
\end{aligned}
\]
The given area is exactly \(2002\). Since no triangle can exceed its own bound, their sum reaches this bound only if every triangle reaches its bound. Thus all four angles at \(P\) are right angles.

The Pythagorean theorem now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
AB&=\sqrt{24^2+32^2}=40,\\
BC&=\sqrt{32^2+28^2}=4\sqrt{113},\\
CD&=\sqrt{28^2+45^2}=53,\\
DA&=\sqrt{45^2+24^2}=51.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the perimeter is
\[
40+4\sqrt{113}+53+51
=4(36+\sqrt{113}),
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses elementary triangle area, perpendicular distance, equality in summed bounds, and the Pythagorean theorem.

methods.label: Compare the diagonals
methods.explanation:
Let \(O\) be the intersection of the diagonals. Convexity ensures that \(O\) lies inside the quadrilateral. Using \(AC\) as the common base of triangles \(ABC\) and \(ADC\), their heights are at most \(BO\) and \(DO\), respectively. Thus the area \(K\) satisfies
\[
K\le \frac12 AC(BO+DO)
=\frac12 AC\cdot BD.
\]
Equality holds exactly when the diagonals are perpendicular.

The paths from opposite vertices through \(P\) also give
\[
AC\le PA+PC=52,
\qquad BD\le PB+PD=77.
\]
Combining these bounds with the given area yields
\[
2002=K\le\frac12 AC\cdot BD
\le\frac12\cdot52\cdot77=2002.
\]
Every inequality must therefore be an equality. In particular, \(AC=52\), \(BD=77\), and the diagonals are perpendicular. Equality in \(AC\le AP+PC\) means that \(P\) lies on segment \(AC\); equality in the other diagonal bound puts \(P\) on segment \(BD\). Hence \(P=O\), so the four radial triangles are right triangles.

Applying the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
\begin{aligned}
AB&=\sqrt{24^2+32^2}=40,\\
BC&=\sqrt{32^2+28^2}=4\sqrt{113},\\
CD&=\sqrt{28^2+45^2}=53,\\
DA&=\sqrt{45^2+24^2}=51.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their sum is \(144+4\sqrt{113}=4(36+\sqrt{113})\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
